name: EFC (I) Ltd
tagline: Coworking/flex-office platform trading at an optically cheap P/E that the community argues is inflated by non-cash Ind AS 116 lease accounting
business_overview: Leases and acquires commercial office space, converting it into flexible serviced workspaces (coworking) for corporates, SMEs, MSMEs and startups; expanded via multiple new-vertical subsidiaries (Whitehills Interior, Synthiko, TCC) later folded back via merger.
fundamentals_table: Rs 192 current, near the Rs 171 low (range Rs 171-337)
Q1FY27 revenue Rs 282.88 Cr, PAT +58.91% YoY
fundamentals_narrative: Headline ROE/growth numbers look excellent and the 11.1x P/E looks cheap, but the community's accounting-quality critique below argues normalized PAT is materially lower than reported.
sentiment_summary: Read most recent 50 of 255 posts (Dec 2025 to June 2026), spanning a controversial related-entity merger, a dilutive QIP announced near 52-week lows, and a detailed accounting-quality critique of the company's lease treatment.
community_signal: A Moneylife article (relayed by yogeshkhadse) reports proxy advisor SES publicly questioned the logic of EFC's merger with its own recently-incorporated subsidiary Whitehills Interior Ltd (WIL) despite shareholder approval. Shivam_Mahana and sanju.inlv flagged a QIP announced at/near 52-week lows as dilutive, with Aloysius_De_Sa (trusted) explicitly calling it 'nonsensical.' Most significantly, rkochatterjee (2 detailed posts, June 2026) laid out that under Ind AS 116, EFC recognizes the full present value of long-term lease contracts as revenue upfront (a non-cash 'Lease receivable recognition' item of Rs 182.81 Cr flowing through operating cash flow), and that normalized PAT once this is stripped out could be as low as ~Rs 100 Cr against a reported Rs 235 Cr FY26 PAT - implying a real P/E closer to 26x, not the optically cheap 11x. hnk_so (trusted) corroborated this read.
bull_case: Reported ROE of 34.3% and Q1FY27 PAT growth of 58.91% YoY are genuinely strong if taken at face value
GCC/managed-office demand tailwind is real and independently corroborated by peer companies' concalls and a Deloitte forecast of 5,000 new GCCs
Promoter has historically been aggressive on growth/expansion into adjacent verticals (BESS, data centers via Synthiko)
bear_case: Community-documented accounting-quality concern: Ind AS 116 finance-lease treatment may inflate reported PAT by more than 2x versus a cash-adjusted normalized figure, which would make the stock materially more expensive than its headline P/E suggests

A related-entity merger (Whitehills Interior) was publicly challenged by an independent proxy advisor as lacking clear strategic logic, alongside a pattern of spinning out new promoter-heavy subsidiaries
QIP announced near 52-week lows dilutes existing shareholders at an inopportune price, with even a trusted community member calling the timing 'nonsensical'
Occupancy/seat-addition targets have already been walked back once (92k seats FY26 target cut to ~78-80k)
verdict_headline: Optically cheap on reported numbers, but a specific and detailed community accounting-quality critique plus a proxy-advisor-challenged merger and dilutive QIP warrant real caution
verdict_reasoning: A specific, quantified community critique (not vague suspicion) argues normalized PAT is roughly half of reported PAT, which would more than double the real P/E
Independent corroboration from a second trusted user, plus a proxy advisor publicly challenging a related-entity merger, raises this above a single-poster concern
Dilutive capital raising near 52-week lows compounds rather than offsets the governance/accounting caution
red_flag_reason: Community-documented accounting-quality concern (Ind AS 116 lease revenue recognition potentially overstating PAT by 2x+), a proxy-advisor-challenged related-entity merger (Whitehills Interior), and a dilutive QIP announced near 52-week lows - a cluster of governance/transparency signals, not a single isolated concern.

trusted_signals.note: "Invested and Biased with 2% allocation" (post #214) while sharing quarterly results.
